chief_complaint: severe fatigue, pale skin, cold hands, and heavy menstrual bleeding
hpi_details: 24F reports 6 months of worsening fatigue, feeling out of breath when climbing stairs, cold hands/feet, and pale skin. Mentions her menstrual periods are very heavy, lasting 7-8 days and requiring double pads.
ideas: thinks she is just overworked and needs iron supplements
concerns: worried about leukemia or blood cancer

clinical_knowledge.topic: Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia (secondary to menorrhagia) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia (secondary to menorrhagia) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management follows an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for severe iron deficiency anemia secondary to menorrhagia, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Heavy, prolonged menstrual periods (menorrhagia) requiring double pads
Progressive fatigue and exertional breathlessness over 6 months
Pallor and cold extremities suggesting significant anemia
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia (secondary to menorrhagia).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Anemia of chronic disease without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Chest pain or severe breathlessness — may need urgent transfusion if anemia is severe.
management_principles: Order CBC (microcytic anemia), ferritin, iron panel
Start oral Ferrous Sulfate 325mg daily with Vitamin C
Refer to gynecology for evaluation and management of menorrhagia
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 24F with 6 months of worsening fatigue, exertional breathlessness, cold hands/feet, and pale skin, in the setting of heavy menstrual periods lasting 7-8 days and requiring double pads.
reference_soap.objective: Pale conjunctiva and pale skin. Mild tachycardia. Cool extremities. No koilonychia noted.
reference_soap.assessment: Severe iron deficiency anemia secondary to menorrhagia.
reference_soap.plan: Order CBC (microcytic anemia), ferritin, iron panel. Start oral Ferrous Sulfate 325mg daily with Vitamin C. Refer to gynecology for evaluation of menorrhagia and provide comprehensive patient counseling.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia secondary to menorrhagia.
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for severe fatigue, pale skin, cold hands, and heavy menstrual bleeding
Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for hematology & oncology
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies for Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia secondary to menorrhagia.

teaching.diagnosis: Severe Iron Deficiency Anemia (secondary to menorrhagia)
teaching.one_liner: Chronic blood loss from heavy periods depletes iron stores faster than they can be replaced, causing fatigue, pallor, and cold extremities from reduced oxygen-carrying capacity.
differentials: GI blood loss (if menstrual history doesn't fully explain it)
red_flags: Chest pain or severe breathlessness — may need urgent transfusion if anemia is severe

must_ask.say: How many days do your periods last, and how often do you need to change pads?
How long have you been feeling this tired?
Do you get short of breath going up stairs?
Have your hands and feet felt unusually cold, or has your skin looked pale?
How much iron-rich food, like red meat, do you typically eat?
